report:
Oracle Debezium - Schema changes causing restart

Hi,
Currently we are trying to replicate some tables from an Oracle database to Postgres database. We are running Debezium version 2.2.0.Final. These connector is set up on AWS MSK and we are using AWS Glue Schema Registry.
What we've noticed is that when we have inserts or updates, data is being replicated fine. Our issue is with the below:
When the source table is altered, the connector fails with a data exception, forcing the connector to restart, creates a new version of the schema on AWS Glue and sends all records of the source table to kafka (not just the record after the schema was changed).
Below is the configuration that we are using:
buffer.memory=20000
connector.class=io.debezium.connector.oracle.OracleConnector
database.dbname=******
database.hostname=******
database.password=******
database.pdb.name=******
database.port=******
database.server.name=******
database.user=******
decimal.handling.mode=string
errors.log.enable=true
errors.log.include.messages=true
key.converter.avroRecordType=GENERIC_RECORD
key.converter.compatibility=FORWARD
key.converter.region=eu-central-1
key.converter.registry.name=testKey
key.converter.schemaAutoRegistrationEnabled=true
key.converter.schemas.enable=true
key.converter=org.apache.kafka.connect.storage.StringConverter
lob.enabled=true
log.mining.strategy=online_catalog
offset.flush.timeout.ms=20000
schema.history.internal.consumer.sasl.client.callback.handler.class=software.amazon.msk.auth.iam.IAMClientCallbackHandler
schema.history.internal.consumer.sasl.jaas.config=software.amazon.msk.auth.iam.IAMLoginModule required;
schema.history.internal.consumer.sasl.mechanism=AWS_MSK_IAM
schema.history.internal.consumer.security.protocol=SASL_SSL
schema.history.internal.kafka.bootstrap.servers=******
schema.history.internal.kafka.topic=******
schema.history.internal.producer.sasl.client.callback.handler.class=software.amazon.msk.auth.iam.IAMClientCallbackHandler
schema.history.internal.producer.sasl.jaas.config=software.amazon.msk.auth.iam.IAMLoginModule required;
schema.history.internal.producer.sasl.mechanism=AWS_MSK_IAM
schema.history.internal.producer.security.protocol=SASL_SSL
schema.history.internal.store.only.captured.tables.ddl=true
schema.include.list=schematest
snapshot.mode=always
table.include.list=schematest.test
tasks.max=1
topic.prefix=db.setup
transforms=dropPrefix
transforms.dropPrefix.regex=([^.]+).([^.]+).([^.]+).([^.]+)
transforms.dropPrefix.replacement=$4
transforms.dropPrefix.type=org.apache.kafka.connect.transforms.RegexRouter
transforms.unwrap.type=io.debezium.transforms.ExtractNewRecordState
value.converter.avroRecordType=GENERIC_RECORD
value.converter.compatibility=FORWARD
value.converter.region=eu-central-1
value.converter.registry.name=testValue
value.converter.schemaAutoRegistrationEnabled=true
value.converter.schemas.enable=true
value.converter=com.amazonaws.services.schemaregistry.kafkaconnect.AWSKafkaAvroConverter
Can anyone let us know if there's a way to keep the connector from doing a restart and just updates the schema registry version? Or otherwise, after restart if it's able to send only the records inserted after the database schema change?
Thanks in advance,
Kurt

evidence.quote: You see a re-snapshot every connector restart because of \"snapshot.mode=always\"."; Kurt Aquilina: "Thanks Chris that worked

notes: Full re-send after a schema-change-induced restart is snapshot.mode=always doing what it says; follow-up 'Struct{ID=9}' key was a StringConverter misconfiguration. Snapshotter logic settles it.
